definition: Speculate means to form ideas about something without firm evidence — to turn over possibilities that cannot yet be checked.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word speculate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know speculate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: With the CEO saying nothing, analysts could only speculate about who would be named to succeed her.
Wonder is milder than speculate: wondering is an open question drifting by, while speculating sits down with the question and starts building actual possibilities.
Fantasize goes further than speculate — speculation at least aims at what might really be true, but fantasy cuts the tether and spins scenes it never expects the world to honor.

To guess is to pick an answer with little basis and less ceremony — one shot, offered and done. Speculating is sustained: you raise possibilities, turn them over, build little stories — still without real evidence.
To theorize is to build a reasoned framework that's meant to be tested against evidence. Speculation floats freer: ideas offered with no way — or no intention — of testing them yet.

Speculate means to form ideas about something without firm evidence — to turn over possibilities that cannot yet be checked.

For sixty years the town speculated about the courthouse cornerstone: the founders had sealed something inside it in 1907, and every generation floated its own theory — deeds, love letters, a bottle of rye — until a renovation crew finally cut the stone open and found a single photograph nobody could identify.

Speculate fits because sixty years of theories ran on no evidence at all — the stone was sealed, so every idea was as uncheckable as the next, and that is the word's core: thought roaming past what can be verified.
The moment the saw went in, speculation ended and facts took over.
Unlike this unit's surmise, which builds one likely conclusion out of real clues, speculating multiplies possibilities precisely because there are no clues to build from.
Speculate is at home wherever information runs out — newsrooms, trading floors, group chats — and it always concedes its own weakness: to say people are speculating is to say they don't know.
Among this unit's guessing verbs, surmise reasons from clues and posit stakes a claim for argument's sake; speculate does neither, and just roams.
In finance the word grows teeth: to speculate is to bet money on an uncertain market, risk included by definition.
